surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Misa sparks the Sharks back from two down
paras: Montréal had a goal taken off after a video review early in the first. Macklin Celebrini struck first for the Sharks late in the period, but Nick Suzuki tied it up for Montréal less than three minutes later. Juraj Slafkovský put the Canadiens up 2-1 early in the second. Cole Caufield made it 3-1 late in the period, but Michael Misa cut Montréal’s lead to 3-2 early in the third. Tyler Toffoli made it 3-3 on the power play midway through the period. Celebrini won it with his second goal of the night on the power play a little over two minutes into overtime. That disallowed goal stung: the game went to overtime. Celebrini added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Alex Nedeljkovic made 31 saves for the Sharks, and Jakub Dobeš stopped 26 of 30. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Phillip Danault, even in a loss and with Celebrini’s overtime winner in the game, by our Swing measure.
A scrum midway through the second sent four players to the box. The Canadiens hit two posts and the crossbar twice and came up a goal short. The Sharks moved to 5-4-1, and the Habs dropped to 4-3-2.

items.text: Michael Misa scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 16.
With Alexander Wennberg out, Collin Graf took his spot and won 4 of 6 faceoffs.
The Sharks bounced back after two straight losses.
